question: When was the cement industry in India totally decontrolled?
solution:
The correct answer is **1989**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Decontrol of the Cement Industry**: The cement industry in India was totally decontrolled in **1989**.
 
• **Economic Liberalization**: This move was part of broader economic liberalization efforts to boost industrial growth.
 
• **Pricing Freedom**: Decontrol allowed cement producers to set their own prices, leading to increased competition.
 
• **Increased Production**: The decontrol led to a significant increase in cement production capacity in India.
 
• **Market Dynamics**: The decision to decontrol was aimed at improving market dynamics and ensuring better availability of cement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Aspect
 Description
 
 
 
 

 **Cement Industry**
 The cement industry is crucial for infrastructure development and economic growth.
 
 

 **Decontrol**
 Decontrol refers to the removal of government controls and regulations, allowing for market-driven decisions.
 
 

 **Economic Reforms**
 India’s economic reforms in the late 1980s and early 1990s aimed at liberalizing the economy.
 
 

 **Industrial Growth**
 Decontrol of industries like cement was intended to spur industrial growth and competitiveness.
 
 

 **Market Competition**
 Increased competition post-decontrol often leads to better quality and pricing for consumers.
